dimension_assessments.summary: Runtime-generated and non-pointer interaction callers are not reconciled with the static catalog/matrix checks; the readiness-report projector/watcher consumer is also not assigned.
Missing/corrupt/stale report states, disabled-reason replacement, and pending or failed command projection states are unspecified.
Report-to-dispatch TOCTOU, replay/deduplication, command ordering, and multi-event atomicity are not closed.
Report replacement, queue delivery, and partial multi-event append failures lack normative outcomes.
Retry, deduplication, crash recovery, projection recovery, cancellation, and recovery from a defective gate are not defined.
The view/domain separation is strong, but independent handler authorization and command-context binding are absent.
Persistent command/event data and exposed blocker metadata have no classification, minimization, protection, retention, or deletion rules.
Report strings and command args lack validation and bounds, and the `/lenient` token is schema-ambiguous.
The false gate is explicitly fail-closed, but races, report failures, stale reasons, and projection lag can still make visible state untrue.
No offline, disconnect, channel-closure, retry, or eventual-delivery behavior is specified for dispatcher traffic or projected feedback.
No queue capacity, input size/depth, blocker count/length, runtime surface count, or backpressure bounds are defined.
Disabled reasons and non-pointer/composite interactions lack assistive-technology discovery, announcements, focus, and activation semantics.
Raw reason/path/ID projection has no localized template or rule separating translated prose from stable machine identifiers.
Envelope/payload versioning, stage-aware handler status, migration proof execution, and the webextract enum token remain underspecified.
Correlation exists, but command lifecycle, report generation, queue status, projection lag, retry, and gate-tool remediation are not required as support-visible telemetry.
No risk-tiered confirmation, authorization, preview, undo, or recovery contract augments the universal dispatch rule.
Handler-stage semantics and owner-document consumer edges lack sufficiently explicit mechanically verified seam contracts.
Static coverage cannot prove runtime surface coverage, event tests are type-only, and lint soundness boundaries are not specified.
Dynamic/plugin/agent surfaces, multi-window causality, continuous-control semantics, verifier failure, and ambiguous extension tokens expose unbounded behavior not closed by this window.
